input.passage: Sea otters often float on their backs while they eat. An otter will place a flat rock on its chest and strike a clam against ______ the shell cracks open after a few hits.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: "until the shell cracks open after a few hits"는 종속절이므로 앞의 독립절에 문장부호 없이 바로 이어져야 하며, 따라서 A가 정답이다. B는 문장 끝에 오는 필수 종속절 앞에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 수식 관계를 끊는다. C는 "Until the shell cracks open after a few hits."를 독립된 문장으로 만들어 문장 조각(fragment)을 남긴다. D의 세미콜론은 두 독립절 사이에만 쓸 수 있는데, 뒤의 내용은 종속절이므로 틀렸다.
input.explanation_en: The words "until the shell cracks open after a few hits" form a dependent clause, so they should attach directly to the main clause with no punctuation. That makes A correct. B puts an unnecessary comma before a dependent clause that is essential to the meaning at the end of the sentence. C turns "Until the shell cracks open after a few hits." into its own sentence, which leaves a fragment. D is wrong because a semicolon can only join two independent clauses, and the part after it is dependent.
input.design: 이 문항은 easy 수준으로 설계했다. 종속접속사 until이 이끄는 절의 경계라는 규칙 하나만 알면 풀 수 있으며, 오답은 쉼표, 마침표, 세미콜론을 잘못 쓰는 전형적인 오개념으로 구성했다.

input.passage: In the early 1800s, most workers in Lowell, Massachusetts, labored in textile mills for more than twelve hours a day. Many of these workers were young women from nearby farms ______ they formed some of the first labor organizations in the United States to demand shorter hours.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.design: 빈칸 앞뒤가 모두 독립절인 단순 구조로, 쉼표+등위접속사 규칙 하나만 알면 풀 수 있게 만들었다. 오답은 쉼표 스플라이스, 융합문(run-on), 접속사 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣는 전형적인 실수로 구성했다.
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 "Many of these workers were young women from nearby farms"와 뒤의 "they formed ... shorter hours"는 둘 다 독립절이다. 독립절 두 개는 쉼표와 등위접속사로 이어야 하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. B는 아무 문장부호나 접속사 없이 두 절을 붙인 융합문이다. C는 "and" 뒤에 불필요한 쉼표를 넣어 문장 흐름을 끊는다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank ("Many of these workers were young women from nearby farms") and the text after it ("they formed ... shorter hours") are both independent clauses. To join two independent clauses, you can use a comma followed by a coordinating conjunction, so D is correct. A uses only a comma, which creates a comma splice. B puts the two clauses together with no punctuation or conjunction at all, which makes a run-on sentence. C adds an unnecessary comma after "and" that breaks up the sentence.

input.passage: In 1959, engineers in the Netherlands began building a set of large storm-surge barriers along the country's southwestern coast. The project took nearly four decades to ______ the final barrier, a pair of enormous swinging gates near Rotterdam, was completed in 1997.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The project took nearly four decades to finish"와 뒤 "the final barrier ... was completed in 1997"은 각각 독립절이다. 두 독립절을 이으려면 세미콜론 같은 강한 경계가 필요하고, 접속부사 indeed 뒤에는 쉼표를 찍으므로 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 문장부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 무종지문(run-on)이다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "The project took nearly four decades to finish," is an independent clause, and so is the text after it, "the final barrier ... was completed in 1997." Joining two independent clauses takes a strong boundary such as a semicolon, and the transition word "indeed" is followed by a comma, so A is correct. B and D join the two independent clauses with only commas, which makes a comma splice. C has no punctuation at all, which makes a run-on sentence.
input.design: 독립절 두 개 사이 경계 하나만 판단하면 되는 쉬운 문항이다. 오답은 흔한 오개념인 쉼표 스플라이스 두 가지와 무종지문으로 구성했다.

input.passage: In Ellen Marsh's novel The Lamplighter's Daughter, young Clara spends her evenings at the window of her aunt's narrow house, watching the fog roll in from the harbor. One night she sees a stranger standing beneath the gas lamp across the ______ he is holding a letter addressed to her late mother.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "One night she sees a stranger standing beneath the gas lamp across the street"와 뒤 "he is holding a letter addressed to her late mother"는 모두 독립절이다. 접속사 없이 두 독립절을 연결하려면 세미콜론이 필요하므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 아무 문장부호 없이 두 절을 붙여 무종지문(run-on)이 된다. D의 "and so"는 인과 관계를 나타내는데, 낯선 사람이 서 있다는 사실이 편지를 들고 있는 이유가 되지 않으므로 논리에 맞지 않는다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "One night she sees a stranger standing beneath the gas lamp across the street," and the text after it, "he is holding a letter addressed to her late mother," are both independent clauses. When two independent clauses are joined without a conjunction, you need a semicolon, so B is correct. A uses only a comma, which creates a comma splice. C uses no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence. D adds "and so," which signals cause and effect, but the stranger standing there is not the reason he is holding the letter, so the logic doesn't work.
input.design: 독립절 두 개가 명확히 보이는 문장에서 세미콜론과 쉼표 스플라이스·무종지문·부적절한 접속을 구분하는 한 가지 규칙만 요구하도록 easy 수준으로 구성했다.

input.passage: The Atacama Desert in northern Chile is one of the driest places on Earth. Some weather stations there have recorded almost no rain for decades ______ scientists use the region to test equipment designed for exploring Mars.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.design: 독립절 두 개 사이의 쉼표+등위접속사 규칙 하나만 묻는 easy 문항. 오답은 쉼표 스플라이스, 런온, 쉼표 위치 오류라는 전형적 오개념으로 구성했다.
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "Some weather stations ... for decades"와 빈칸 뒤 "scientists use the region ..."는 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 쉼표와 등위접속사로 연결해야 하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 독립절을 연결한 쉼표 스플라이스이다. B는 아무 문장부호나 접속사 없이 두 절을 이어 붙인 런온 문장이다. D는 접속사가 있지만 쉼표가 "and" 앞이 아닌 뒤에 와서 잘못된 위치에 놓였다.
input.explanation_en: The part before the blank ("Some weather stations ... for decades") and the part after it ("scientists use the region ...") each have their own subject and verb, so both are independent clauses. To join two independent clauses, you need a comma followed by a coordinating conjunction, so C is correct. A is a comma splice because it joins the clauses with only a comma. B is a run-on sentence because it has no punctuation or conjunction at all. D does include "and," but the comma belongs before the conjunction, not after it.

input.passage: Sea otters often wrap themselves in strands of kelp before they fall asleep. The long, flexible seaweed acts like an anchor ______ it keeps the resting otters from drifting away from their feeding grounds while the tide moves around them.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.design: 빈칸 양쪽이 모두 독립절이라 세미콜론 하나만 알면 풀리는 easy 문항이다. 오답은 쉼표 스플라이스, 무부호 융합문, 접속사 뒤 불필요한 쉼표로 구성했다.
input.explanation: 빈칸 앞 "The long, flexible seaweed acts like an anchor"와 빈칸 뒤 "it keeps the resting otters..."는 각각 주어와 동사를 갖춘 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결할 수 있으므로 B가 정답이다. A는 쉼표만으로 두 독립절을 이어 쉼표 스플라이스가 된다. C는 아무 부호 없이 두 독립절을 붙인 융합문이다. D는 접속사 "and" 뒤에 쉼표를 넣어 "and"와 이어지는 절 사이를 불필요하게 끊는다.
input.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "The long, flexible seaweed acts like an anchor," and the text after it, "it keeps the resting otters...," are both independent clauses, since each has its own subject and verb. A semicolon can join two independent clauses, so B is correct. A joins the two clauses with only a comma, which makes a comma splice. C puts the two clauses together with no punctuation at all, which creates a run-on sentence. D adds a comma after the conjunction "and," which wrongly separates "and" from the clause it introduces.

input.passage: In the late nineteenth century, public libraries spread rapidly across many British towns. Supported by local taxes, these libraries offered free access to books for factory workers who could not afford to buy them. The reading rooms in the library at Leeds ______ especially popular with workers in the evenings, when they finished their shifts.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.design: Easy subject-verb agreement with a short prepositional phrase ("in the library at Leeds") between the plural subject and the verb; past tense is clearly set by "late nineteenth century."
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 "reading rooms"이므로 복수 동사가 필요하고, 지문은 19세기 후반을 묘사하므로 과거 시제여야 합니다. 따라서 D가 정답입니다. A는 과거 시제지만 단수형이라, 동사 바로 앞의 "library"나 "Leeds"를 주어로 착각할 때 고르기 쉬운 오답입니다. B는 단수형이고 현재 시제입니다. C도 단수형이며 지문의 과거 시점과 맞지 않습니다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "reading rooms," so you need a plural verb, and since the passage describes the late nineteenth century, the verb should be in the past tense. That makes D the correct answer. A is past tense but singular, so it's an easy trap if you mistake "library" or "Leeds," the words right before the verb, for the subject. B is singular and in the present tense. C is also singular, and it doesn't fit the passage's past time frame.

input.passage: Sea otters play an important role in kelp forest ecosystems along the Pacific coast. Each otter eats large numbers of sea urchins, which graze on kelp. When otters are present, the population of urchins near the shore ______ small enough for kelp forests to grow tall and provide shelter for many species of fish.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'the population'이고, 'of urchins near the shore'는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 단수 동사가 필요하며, 지문의 다른 동사(eat, graze, are)처럼 현재 시제를 쓰는 B 'remains'가 정답이다. A 'remain', C 'have remained', D 'are remaining'은 모두 복수 동사로, 바로 앞의 복수 명사 'urchins'나 'shore'와 잘못 일치시킨 것이다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this clause is the singular noun "the population"; the phrase "of urchins near the shore" just modifies it. So the verb has to be singular, and B, "remains," is correct. It's also in the present tense, which fits the passage's other verbs ("eats," "graze," "are"). Choices A ("remain"), C ("have remained"), and D ("are remaining") are all plural verb forms. They mistakenly agree with the nearby plural noun "urchins" instead of with the actual subject.
input.design: 수식 전치사구가 짧게 끼어든 주어-동사 수 일치 하나만 묻도록 구성했으며, 오답은 근처 복수 명사에 끌린 전형적 오류이다.

input.passage: Located in northern Chile, the Atacama Desert is one of the driest places on Earth. Some weather stations there have recorded almost no rainfall for decades. Each year, the cold ocean current that flows along the nearby coast ______ moist air from forming the clouds that would bring rain inland.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 빈칸의 동사는 단수 주어 'the cold ocean current'와 수가 일치해야 하므로, 단수 동사 C 'prevents'가 정답이다. 'that flows along the nearby coast'는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐 동사의 수에 영향을 주지 않는다. A 'prevent', B 'have prevented', D 'are preventing'은 모두 복수 동사이므로 단수 주어와 맞지 않는다. 바로 앞의 'coast'가 아니라 핵심 주어 'current'를 기준으로 판단해야 한다.
input.explanation_en: The verb in the blank has to agree with the singular subject "the cold ocean current," so the singular verb in C, "prevents," is correct. The phrase "that flows along the nearby coast" just describes the subject, so it doesn't change whether the verb is singular or plural. A ("prevent"), B ("have prevented"), and D ("are preventing") are all plural verb forms, so none of them agrees with a singular subject. Make sure you match the verb to the main subject, "current," not to the nearest noun, "coast."
input.design: 짧은 관계절 수식어가 붙은 단수 주어와 동사의 수 일치라는 규칙 하나만 묻도록 만들었다. 오답은 모두 복수형이어서, 규칙을 알면 바로 배제할 수 있다.

input.passage: In Elena Marsh's novel The Lamplighter's Daughter, a modern story told in the style of a nineteenth-century novel, young Clara Whitby lives in a foggy harbor town. Every evening, the old letters hidden in her grandmother's writing desk ______ Clara to imagine the lives of sailors who never came home.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수 명사 'letters'이므로 복수 동사가 필요하다. C의 'inspire'는 복수 주어와 수가 일치하므로 정답이다. A의 'inspires', B의 'has inspired', D의 'is inspiring'은 모두 단수 동사이다. 이 선택지들은 동사 바로 앞에 있는 단수 명사 'desk'에 잘못 맞춘 것이다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "letters," so the verb has to be plural. C, "inspire," is a plural verb, so it agrees with the subject and is the correct answer. A ("inspires"), B ("has inspired"), and D ("is inspiring") are all singular verbs. They wrongly agree with "desk," the singular noun that comes right before the blank, instead of with "letters."
input.design: 짧은 전치사구 수식어(hidden in her grandmother's writing desk)가 붙은 주어와 동사의 수 일치라는 규칙 하나만 묻는다. 오답 세 개는 모두 단수형이라 가까운 명사 'desk'에 이끌린 학생이 고르기 쉽다.

input.passage: The Okavango Delta in Botswana is unusual because its river never reaches the sea. Instead, the water spreads across the Kalahari Desert and slowly disappears into the sand and air. Each year, floodwaters from the highlands of Angola ______ the delta during the dry season, creating a huge green wetland where elephants, hippos, and many bird species gather.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 복수명사 "floodwaters"이고, "from the highlands of Angola"는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 그러므로 동사는 복수형이어야 하며, "Each year"가 반복되는 사실을 나타내므로 단순현재형인 D "fill"이 정답이다. A "fills", B "has filled", C "is filling"은 모두 단수 동사여서, 바로 앞의 단수명사 "Angola"를 주어로 잘못 본 학생이 고를 수 있는 오답이다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the plural noun "floodwaters," and "from the highlands of Angola" is only a phrase that describes it. That means the verb has to be plural, and because "Each year" points to something that happens again and again, the simple present plural verb in D, "fill," is correct. A ("fills"), B ("has filled"), and C ("is filling") are all singular verbs. You might pick one of them if you mistook the singular noun "Angola," which sits right before the blank, for the subject.
input.design: 이 문항은 짧은 전치사구가 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있는 상황에서 주어-동사 수 일치라는 한 가지 규칙만 묻도록 설계했다. 오답 3개는 모두 단수 동사로 구성해, 빈칸 바로 앞의 단수명사에 이끌리는 전형적인 오개념을 노렸다.

content.text: Easy 수준 문항: 짧은 수식어가 붙은 주어와 동사의 수 일치.

input.passage: In 2019, engineers in the Netherlands installed a footbridge made almost entirely of recycled plastic over a canal in the city of Zwolle. The bridge, built from thousands of discarded bottles and cups, ______ about one-quarter as much as a comparable steel bridge, so it can be lifted into place with a small crane.
input.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
input.explanation: 이 문장의 주어는 단수 명사 'The bridge'이고, 'built from thousands of discarded bottles and cups'는 주어를 꾸미는 수식어일 뿐이다. 따라서 동사는 단수형이어야 하며, 일반적 사실을 진술하는 현재 시제 'weighs'인 A가 정답이다. B 'weigh', C 'are weighing', D 'have weighed'는 모두 복수 동사로, 바로 앞 복수 명사 'bottles and cups'에 잘못 일치시킨 것이다.
input.explanation_en: The subject of this sentence is the singular noun "The bridge." The phrase "built from thousands of discarded bottles and cups" just describes the subject. That means the verb has to be singular, and the simple present "weighs" in A fits a general fact, so A is correct. B ("weigh"), C ("are weighing"), and D ("have weighed") are all plural verb forms. They wrongly agree with the nearby plural noun "bottles and cups" instead of the real subject.
input.design: 짧은 분사 수식어가 단수 주어와 동사 사이에 끼어 있어, 주어-동사 수 일치라는 한 가지 규칙만으로 풀 수 있게 했다. 오답은 모두 가까운 복수 명사에 맞춘 복수형으로, 흔히 하는 실수를 노렸다.
